thread.title: Weekend roundup: Pushing back against Apple and Google | Threat to discount brokers | Why investors don't worry about Manafort and Cohen

author: morningstar.com
title: Weekend roundup: Pushing back against Apple and Google | Threat to discount brokers | Why investors don't worry about Manafort and Cohen
text:
By Philip van Doorn, MarketWatch
How you might save money on smartphone content
MarketWatch rounds up 10 of its most interesting topics over the past week.
1. Maybe a 30% cut is too much
Apple (AAPL) and Google (the main subsidiary of Alphabet (GOOGL)(GOOGL)) often take a 30% cut when you purchase content through the iPhone App Store or Google Play. Netflix (NFLX), Spotify (SPOT) and other companies are pushing back, and it might save you money (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-is-the-latest-company-to-try-bypassing-apples-app-store-2018-08-23).
2. If you can't beat discount brokers, join them
Charles Schwab (SCHW) and other discount brokers changed the game by offering cut-rate services to investors. Decades later, J.P. Morgan Chase (JPM) might be starting a trend as it fights to regain market share by offering free trades (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/discount-broker-stocks-dive-on-news-jp-morgan-chase-to-offer-free-trading-2018-08-21).
3. investors shrug off Trump's latest legal woes
Here's why stock investors don't seem worried (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-why-the-stock-market-remains-immune-to-trumps-legal-woes-2018-08-22) about the multiple convictions of Paul Manafort, President Trump's former campaign chairman and the guilty please of Michael Cohen, the president's former lawyer.
4. Aretha Franklin shows what you need
When Aretha Franklin died on Aug. 16, she left no will. Here's why it is very important for you to have one (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/like-many-americans-aretha-franklin-didnt-have-a-will-2018-08-22).
5. Retail's on fire
Jeff Reeves highlights seven retail stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-seven-stocks-prove-that-retail-is-roaring-2018-08-23) that illustrate the excellent investment trend for the sector.
Read on:Retailers are hot again -- here are the earnings and sales winners (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/retailers-are-hot-again-here-are-the-earnings-and-sales-winners-2018-08-23)
6. Trump's gift to big banks
Some startling numbers show how the tax cuts signed into law by President Trump in December are giving banks a tremendous boost (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-profits-are-soaring-after-tax-cuts-2018-08-23).
7. Amazon's pharmacy
Read this (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/investors-have-misdiagnosed-amazons-push-into-the-pharmacy-business-2018-08-20) if you believe Amazon.com (AMZN) might wipe out traditional drugstore chains, including Walgreens (WBA).
8. Trump's proposal for corporate reporting
The president has asked the Securities and Exchange Commission to study the effects of a move to semiannual corporate reporting to replace quarterly earnings mania. Here's what this radical change might mean to you as an investor (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/should-companies-move-to-a-semi-annual-reporting-schedule-probably-not-say-analysts-2018-08-17).
9. Who lends $21 trillion to Uncle Sam?
The answer may surprise you (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-who-owns-a-record-2121-trillion-of-us-debt-2018-08-21).
10. The mysterious Ryanair
Ryanair (RYAAY) says it is trying to speed up its boarding process, but the discount airline may only be confusing its customers with its new baggage rules and fees (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ryanairs-latest-fees-for-carry-on-bags-leaves-passengers-confused-annoyed-2018-08-24).

-Philip van Doorn; 1547ET
